newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom says hurt by weak holiday sales.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom says hurt by weak holiday sales.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc said weak holiday sales, higher inventories than planned, higher markdowns and an increase in inventory "shrinkage" contributed to a decline in fourth quarter net income.

Dan Nordstrom, a co-president of the upscale department store chain, said the impact of a merchandise reorganization in women's apparel was mostly behind the company but probably would have "some lingering effects."
"We are pleased with customer response to our stores in promising new markets but disappointed with lower net income," he said in the company's earnings statement.
Nordstrom reported fourth-quarter net income of $0.53 per share -- far below the Wall Street consensus figure of $0.64 and last year's $0.67.

While comparable-store sales rose 5.4 percent in January, they fell 3.8 percent in the crucial month of December and fell 1.3 percent for the quarter. For the year comparable-store sales rose 0.6 percent.
Nordstrom said parts of its holiday merchandising strategy were not executed as well as planned, such as the assortment of gift items.
Nordstrom also cited an increase in inventory "shrinkage", which refers to inventory that is missing, generally due to theft or poor recordkeeping.
The company said results were also hurt by five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas and by severe weather in the weeks after Christmas.
Nordstrom also said higher write-offs on the company's credit card balances contributed to lower net income.
"The credit card write-offs have stabilized in the last three months, although for the past year they were higher than average," Dan Nordstrom said.

He added that the merchandise reorganization "was a necessary move to meet our customers' changing needs and to position ourselves for the long term despite its downward impact on financial results in the short term."

Nordstrom plans to open three new full-line stores opening in the second half of 1997 in Garden City, N.Y., Hartford, Conn., and Cleveland. The company also plans four new Rack discount stores this year.
Nordstrom has a total 83 stores in 17 states.
Nordstrom also said its board of directors had approved a third $100 million common stock repurchase program. In October, the company completed a $100 million stock repurchase approved in May 1995.
Nordstrom has bought $33 million of a second $100 million stock repurchase authorized in November.
